paper_metadata.title: Outcomes of low-dose valproic acid treatment in patients with juvenile myoclonic epilepsy

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a large sample from a specialized epilepsy clinic, providing good internal validity for JME. However, it is a retrospective hospital-based cohort which may introduce referral bias, and the participation rate of the original 290 eligible patients (down to 215) is not fully explained, though baseline characteristics are well-described.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: outpatient clinical records of 290 patients among 5760 patients who underwent follow-up in the Epilepsy Outpatient Clinics of the Department of Neurology at Istanbul University Cerrahpaşa
items.reasoning: The source is a specific tertiary care epilepsy clinic, and the broader population context is provided.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: This retrospective, cross-sectional study reviewed the outpatient clinical records of 290 patients... Finally, the study included 215 patients who met the study inclusion criteria.
items.reasoning: While the source is clear, the transition from 290 to 215 patients is mentioned but the specific reasons for the exclusion of the 75 patients (other than general criteria) are not detailed in a flow-diagram format.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text mentions follow-up durations (mean 9.98 years), but the specific calendar years for the recruitment window are not explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: Epilepsy Outpatient Clinics of the Department of Neurology at Istanbul University Cerrahpaşa, School of Medicine
items.reasoning: The specific clinical setting and institution are clearly identified.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria were as follows: 1. Unequivocal clinical (historical) evidence of myoclonic jerking... 2. No evidence of a neurological or intellectual deficit... Patients with brain stem injuries due to trauma or infections were excluded
items.reasoning: Detailed clinical, EEG, and imaging-based inclusion/exclusion criteria are provided.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Finally, the study included 215 patients who met the study inclusion criteria.
items.reasoning: 215/290 (74%) of identified JME patients were included. This is slightly below the 80% threshold usually preferred for low risk, but still substantial.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Sex and current age, age at the time of the first seizure, disease duration, and duration of follow up were recorded for each patient.
items.reasoning: Table 1 and the text provide a comprehensive breakdown of demographics and clinical history.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: As a retrospective cross-sectional analysis of a stable follow-up cohort, the study accounts for all 215 patients. It specifically analyzes reasons for relapse and refractoriness, effectively capturing 'attrition' from the state of remission.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Finally, the study included 215 patients who met the study inclusion criteria... All patients were divided into two groups on the basis of remission and refractoriness
items.reasoning: All 215 patients included in the study were accounted for in the final analysis.

items.label: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out
items.prompt: Attempts to collect information on participants who dropped out of the study are described.
items.evidence_snippet: Interviews with patients were conducted either face-to-face (in outpatient clinics) or via telephone.
items.reasoning: The use of telephone interviews to supplement clinic records suggests an active attempt to capture data on those not currently attending in person.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: Factors that may have caused termination of the remission period were evaluated; these included irregular drug use, drug side effects, and drug change or discontinuation
items.reasoning: The study explicitly tracks why patients 'dropped out' of remission, which is the primary prognostic outcome.

items.label: Outcome and prognostic factor information on those lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Participants lost to follow-up are adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The study does not explicitly describe the characteristics of the 75 patients from the original 290 who were not included in the final 215.

items.prompt: There are no important differences between key characteristics (LIST) and outcomes in participants who completed the study and those who did not.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no comparison provided between the included sample and those excluded or lost before the study start.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The primary prognostic factor (VPA dose) is clearly defined and categorized. The use of a 750mg cutoff is clinically relevant, and data availability for the dose was high due to the nature of the clinical records.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: divided into two groups according to the use of low-dose VPA therapy (VPA ≤ 750 mg/day and > 750 mg/day).
items.reasoning: The prognostic factor (VPA dose) is clearly defined with a specific milligram threshold.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Analysis relied on drug doses rather than serum concentrations... recorded for VPA and other AEDs in patients who achieved remission.
items.reasoning: Dose recording from clinical charts is a standard and reliable method in epilepsy research, though it doesn't account for actual adherence (which the authors acknowledge by tracking 'irregular drug use').

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: VPA ≤ 750 mg/day and > 750 mg/day
items.reasoning: The 750mg cutoff is a standard clinical threshold for 'low dose' in VPA literature.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Follow-up by a single neurologist for at least 2 years... A follow-up form was prepared to record clinical and demographic characteristics.
items.reasoning: Standardized data collection by a single center/neurologist ensures consistency.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: The first AED, add-on AEDs, total number of AEDs, onset of VPA therapy, remission and maintenance doses... were recorded.
items.reasoning: The study implies complete records for the 215 included patients.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There is no mention of missing data or imputation methods; it is assumed only patients with complete records were analyzed.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (remission) is defined using standard ILAE-consistent criteria (2 years seizure-free). While it relies on patient recall/diaries, this is the standard of care in epilepsy clinical practice.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Remission was defined as a seizure-free (i.e., myoclonic, absence, and/or GTC) period of at least 2 years.
items.reasoning: The outcome is explicitly defined with a temporal threshold and specific seizure types.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: GTC seizure status as revealed by EEG findings and seizure diaries.
items.reasoning: Seizure diaries are standard but subject to recall bias. There was no blinding of the outcome assessor (the treating neurologist).

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The final clinical examination was performed during face-to-face interviews. A follow-up form was prepared
items.reasoning: All patients were assessed using the same clinical follow-up form and interview process.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study identifies and measures several important confounders (seizure type, psychiatric comorbidities, EEG findings). However, it relies on univariable comparisons (t-tests, chi-square) rather than multivariable modeling to adjust for these factors simultaneously.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: presence of psychiatric illnesses and other comorbid conditions... SE, presence of clinical photosensitivity, photoparoxysmal response (PPR)... triggering factors
items.reasoning: A wide array of clinical and demographic confounders were captured.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: EEG asymmetries were defined as focal slowing, focal epileptiform discharges... asymmetric generalized spike/polyspike/wave discharges
items.reasoning: Technical confounders like EEG findings are well-defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Twenty-one-channel EEG recordings were collected using the international 10–20 electrode placement system.
items.reasoning: Confounders like EEG were measured using standardized, objective medical protocols.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: A follow-up form was prepared to record clinical and demographic characteristics... for each patient.
items.reasoning: Consistency in data collection is maintained across the cohort.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods are used if imputation is used for missing confounder data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: No mention of missing data handling for confounders.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: The patients were divided into remission and refractory groups.
items.reasoning: The study uses group comparison (stratification by outcome) but does not use matching or a prospective design to control for confounders.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: The t-test was used to compare parametric values between groups; the chi-squared test was used to compare categorical variables.
items.reasoning: The analysis is limited to univariable tests. There is no multivariable regression (e.g., Logistic Regression) to adjust for the independent effect of VPA dose while controlling for absence seizures or psychiatric comorbidities.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical analysis is straightforward and appropriate for the descriptive goals of the study. However, the lack of multivariable modeling and the retrospective nature limit the ability to make strong prognostic inferences. Reporting is transparent regarding the results found.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS software, version 22.0... Data are expressed as mean ± standard deviation (SD), median (min–max), number, and frequency.
items.reasoning: The methods section clearly outlines the tests used for each data type.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There was no multivariable model building strategy described.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: The t-test was used to compare parametric values between groups; the chi-squared test was used to compare categorical variables.
items.reasoning: While adequate for a descriptive cross-sectional study, these tests are insufficient for a robust prognosis study which requires adjustment for multiple variables.

items.label: Reporting of results
items.prompt: There is no selective reporting of results.
items.evidence_snippet: Results: Remission was achieved with VPA monotherapy in 116 patients... The dose of VPA was higher in patients with absence seizure... Remission was achieved with a lower dose of VPA in females
items.reasoning: The authors report on all variables mentioned in the methods, including non-significant findings.
